paragraphs: Matya ben Shemuel; another version, Mattityahu, in the Mishnah, beginning of Yoma 3(28a), and Tamid 3. He disagrees with the first tanna; the law follows him, saying, 'Until it is light in Hebron.' He apparently lived toward the Temple's end and supervised its lotteries, as Yoma states; see Menaḥot 100 and Shekalim 5. He was one of fifteen pious men appointed over the Temple. We do not know whether he was a priest: Mordekhai, called Petaḥyah, was also one of them, in charge of bird-offerings, as was the pious R. Neḥunya, well-digger (see his entry). Naḥuma ben Afkashyon, R. Yishmael, R. Akiva and R. Yehudah ben Beteira disagree (see his entry).
